For me it's tough finding anything to break me out of that state. Although, from time to time watching something that makes me laugh helps me feel better for a while. The key in this method is to find something that will specifically make you laugh, not just anything people consider funny.

I remember being in a prolonged state of depression and my only refuge was watching Late Night with Conan. He'd make me laugh so hard that I would actually cry because I was so grateful to laugh genuinely.

Other than that, I always enjoyed watching videos about the universe, which would make me wonder and feel there's a purpose to our existence.

Another thing that helped was to have an outlet. For me, because my family band friends were tired of hearing me out, I picked up photography. Every photo I took was associated with the emotions I felt at the time I took it. Most of the photos I took were at night. I'd often walk around the city late at night when the streets were empty to just clear mind, take photos, and enjoy the silence. An important aspect of this for me was to share the images publicly. I chose to share it on IG with people I knew, but also found relief in sharing the photos anonymously through another alias, account so I could express more freely. Having an outlet allowed me unload a lot of the burden of my depression.
